meanings.note: Material. Common feminine noun meaning 'paper; official document' in everyday Russian.
Colloquial. Common feminine noun meaning 'paper; official document' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here is a document from the prosecutor's office.

examples.text: Вот бумага из прокуратуры. Слушание будет сегодня вечером.
examples.trans: Here is an order from the prosecutor's office. The hearing will be this evening.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Внимание! = Attention!. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А ну-ка, дай посмотрю! Внимание, ребята!
examples.trans: Hold on, let me have a look! Attention, everyone!

Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

давить.gloss: to press, to put pressure on

meanings.note: + на + accusative: давить на совесть = to guilt-trip

examples.text: Не надо мне сейчас на совесть давить.
examples.trans: Don't try to make me feel guilty now.

examples.text: Не надо мне сейчас на совесть давить. Я тебе всё отработала на тех выборах.
examples.trans: Don't try to make me feel guilty now. I paid you back in full at that election.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.
на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'верие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'trust' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The meeting undermined trust in Samsonov.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.en: to get acquainted, to meet (someone new)
meanings.note: 'Давайте знакомиться' = let's introduce ourselves

examples.text: Очень хорошо. Ну что, давайте знакомиться.
examples.trans: Very good. Well then, let's introduce everyone.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'period', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ладно, пусть завтра приходит на испытательный срок.
examples.trans: Alright, let him come tomorrow for a trial period.

examples.text: Денис, уже полчаса, как идёт испытательный срок.
examples.trans: Denis, your trial period started half an hour ago.

meanings.en: by the way, speaking of which
meanings.note: Used as a parenthetical word. Core Russian adv meaning 'by the way; handy' in everyday speech.
Это очень кстати. Core Russian adv meaning 'by the way; handy' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?
Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job
На его место = in his place. Common neuter noun meaning 'place; seat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
+ prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'значать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'I appoint'.

examples.text: Кухня, внимание, я назначаю Лаврова шефом!
examples.trans: Kitchen, attention, I am appointing Lavrov head chef!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и назначать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and I appoint on time.

meanings.note: Назначить на место. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'значить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to set, to appoint', paired with 'назначать'.

Назначить на место. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'значить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to set, to appoint', paired with 'назначать'.
goes right before the word it negates
the person who likes is in the dative: мне нравится = I like it

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to explain', paired with 'объяснять'.

examples.trans: I will explain everything to you right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'optimization' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я составил подробный план оптимизации кухни.
examples.trans: I drew up a detailed kitchen optimization plan.

examples.text: Он даже план оптимизации кухни составил.
examples.trans: He even drew up a kitchen optimization plan.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.

meanings.note: Disappoint expectations. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'вести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to let down, fail', paired with 'подводить'.

examples.trans: I will never let you down.

examples.text: Надёжный друг никогда не подведёт в беде.
examples.trans: A reliable friend will never let you down in trouble.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.
examples.trans: Let us sum up your first work week.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to try, to have a go
meanings.note: + infinitive. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.text: Как я могу это забыть? Ну, давай попробуем.
examples.trans: How can I forget that? Well, let's try.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to continue', paired with 'продолжить'.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.en: to read through, to finish reading
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'читать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to read (through), to finish reading', paired with 'читать'.

examples.trans: I read Machiavelli, that book The Prince.
What else should I read here?

examples.text: Я прочитаю этот рецепт и приготовлю блюдо.
examples.trans: I will read this recipe and prepare the dish.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with
meanings.note: мы сами разберёмся = we'll sort it out ourselves

В + prepositional. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sort out, to figure out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!
Colloquial plural of ребёнок. Common substantive noun meaning 'guys, lads, kids (plural only)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The boys will have a word with you.

examples.text: Тогда ребята с тобой поработают. До свидания, Аркадий Борисович.
examples.trans: Then the boys will have a little word with you. Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').

examples.trans: First they were rude and insulting over there.
Let's start everything from the beginning.

examples.text: Мы танцевали. Сначала они там грубили, оскорбляли.
examples.trans: We were dancing. First they were rude and insulting over there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will you keep (company)'.

examples.trans: How formal, will you keep me company?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и составить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will you keep on time.

related.gloss: not to will you keep (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Второй срок = a second term. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'term, period' in everyday Russian.
Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'term, period' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

meanings.en: to leave on foot, go away

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.
